https://thefrontierpost.com/hungary-expe.text: (AFP/Reuters): Hungary has ordered 10 Russian diplomats to leave the country, accusing them of “unacceptable” activities that it says are incompatible with their diplomatic status. Anita Orban, Hungary’s deputy prime minister and foreign minister, said on Tuesday that the decision to protect “Hungary’s security and sovereignty” does not mean the country is “breaking off diplomatic relations with Russia”. Russia promised a “harsh and painful” response, the country’s Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told Russia’s TASS news agency. Hungary was one of the few European Union allies to Russia after its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Under the previous government, Budapest’s relations with Moscow were warm. Former Prime Minister Viktor Orban (not related to current Deputy Prime Minister Anita Orban), who lost the elections last April after 16 years in power, reportedly told Russian President Vladimir Putin: “I am at your service” during last year’s phone call. Hungary took a “legitimate decision”, EU spokesman Christian Wigand told journalists, adding that the EU “will continue to closely coordinate” the situation. Many EU member states expelled Russian diplomats following Moscow’s all-out war on Ukraine, but Hungary was not one of them until now. Senegal: Footage reveals wreckage of deadly migrant boat in which 39 people died Copy/paste the link below: Copy Copy/paste the article video embed link below: Copy Updated: 10 November 2026 - 9:26 GMT+1 At least 39 people have died after a migrant boat sank off Senegal's Atlantic coast. Footage shows the shattered vessel washed ashore as rescuers continue searching for victims. … More The death toll from a migrant boat sinking off Lompoul, Senegal, has risen to 39 after four more bodies were recovered. The wooden pirogue had departed from Saint-Louis towards Spain's Canary Islands before capsizing on Friday. ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT Footage shows the vessel's hull broken in two on a beach between Dakar and Saint Louis. Emergency services have searched the coastline for three days. Only one survivor has been reported, while the total number aboard remains unknown. Most victims were young people from nearby communities. Regional governor Ndeye Nguenar Mbodj stated that over 20 victims have been identified and returned to relatives. Authorities requested permission to bury four decomposed bodies locally. Teams searched a 25-kilometre stretch of coast, and a judicial investigation has been opened. The tragedy highlights the dangers of the Atlantic migration route to the Canary Islands, where overcrowded fishing boats often undertake lengthy journeys through treacherous waters. Tighter coastal patrols have also contributed to longer and more hazardous crossings from West Africa.
